key_insight: Three data- and gate-informed rules select entanglement structure, circuit depth and readout for variational quantum circuits before training.
engineering_relevance: The approach replaces ansatz-and-depth grid searches with principled design choices, potentially reducing quantum model development costs.
method: Use dataset Fourier-coefficient SVDs to identify needed entanglement and bound the error from omitting it.
Set depth using quantum Fisher information rank growth and its dynamical Lie algebra ceiling.
Estimate all 2^N − 1 Pauli-Z products from one shot batch to maximize directions resolved by single-basis readout.
evidence_signal: On Madelon, the rules selected seven three-qubit blocks at depth three, yielding a 239-parameter classifier with 78.5% test accuracy without grid search; ablations showed lower accuracy with shallower circuits, smaller blocks or no reuploading.
watch_item: Although all Pauli-Z products share a measurement basis, their exponentially growing number raises classical processing and finite-shot precision concerns.
paper_title: Data informed Ansatz Selection for Variational Quantum Circuits
